RFC 021: Serve Multi-route Implementation

RFC 019/020 Execution and Validation

Published

January 19, 2026

Executive Summary

The RFC 019 multi-route serve design and the RFC 020 review adjustments are now implemented in the ingestion service. The implementation adds normalized route parsing, deterministic selection rules, and route-scoped metadata across queues, ledgers, and receipts, while the CLI validates configs with the shared parser and surfaces per-route run metrics. Targeted unit tests confirm defaults, priority routing, queue metadata persistence, and loop behavior.

Implementation Scope

The implementation covers config normalization, routing, queue and receipt metadata, and CLI integration, with test coverage focused on deterministic selection and backward compatible defaults.

Table 1. Implementation scope and evidence.
Area Implementation Evidence
Configuration parsing ServeConfig and ServeRoute parsing with defaults, linting, and legacy migration src/autoclean/utils/ingestion.py
Routing and dispatch Priority and glob-specificity selection with route-aware dispatch plans src/autoclean/utils/ingestion.py
Queue and ledger metadata Route ID and ingestion root persistence in queues and receipts src/autoclean/utils/ingestion.py
CLI validation and reporting Shared config validation and per-route run summaries src/autoclean/cli.py
Unit tests Defaults, priority routing, queue metadata, and loop behavior tests/unit/utils/test_ingestion.py

Configuration and Validation

Serve configuration parsing is centralized in a dedicated parser that enforces known keys, normalizes defaults, and supports legacy single-route configs by wrapping them in a single automation route. The parser derives route identifiers deterministically, validates overlap at equal priority, and keeps disabled routes out of overlap checks, which matches the RFC 020 clarifications. Defaults for file_globs, sentinel_ext, and recursive are applied consistently to ensure uniform routing behavior across routes.

NoteGuardrail

If two enabled routes overlap at the same priority and specificity, the parser fails fast to avoid non-deterministic dispatch.

Routing and Dispatch

Routing assigns each ready file to the highest-priority route that matches both ingestion roots and glob patterns. Glob specificity is scored using literal counts and wildcard depth to make selection deterministic, and any ties at the same priority level are treated as configuration errors. Dispatch is executed per route, ensuring that each route creates a distinct workspace and automation plan while sharing the same runtime definition.

Queue and Provenance Metadata

Queue entries now store the route identifier and the ingestion root used for assignment, which allows replays and retries to preserve the original routing intent. The ingestion ledger and receipts carry the route ID so that deduplication and provenance are scoped per route, reducing the risk of cross-route collisions when the same file structure is reused across pipelines.

CLI Integration

The serve validate command uses the same parser as runtime execution, so linting and defaults are applied consistently. serve run accepts --file-glob and --sentinel-ext as legacy overrides only, and it emits per-route summaries that report ready, processed, and failed counts for operator visibility.

Risks and Deferred Work

The implementation aligns with the RFC 019 model, but several enhancements remain optional depending on operational needs.

Table 3. Risks and deferred work.
Item Rationale Next Step

Glob syntax validation Pattern errors are not validated beyond match results Add pattern sanity checks or precompile validation

Questions and Assumptions

These open choices affect safety, operator burden, and how much validation logic we carry forward. The decisions below reflect the current development posture.

  • Legacy queue entries without route_id: We are still in development, so backward compatibility is not a requirement. Legacy entries should fail fast unless they are explicitly migrated to include route_id.
  • Overlap validation vs. file_globs: Stick with the simple rule. Overlaps at the same priority remain validation errors even if glob patterns appear disjoint.
  • Ingestion root existence in strict mode: Enforce root existence in strict mode. Missing roots should be reported as validation failures rather than deferred to runtime.
